# 01 · At a glance

Live hospital counts come from `data/territoryHospitals.json` (March 2026 CMS TEAM participant extract). Editorial context (Medicare population, HRRP, LEJR) is carried from the published Rainfall guide and is **not** recomputed from claims.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-glance
glance <- tibble::tibble(
  Signal = c("Mandated hospitals", "CBSAs", "Medicare beneficiaries", "HRRP", "Est. annual LEJR"),
  Value = c(
    as.character(SCOPE_N),
    as.character(SCOPE_CBSA_N),
    editorial$medicare,
    editorial$hrrp,
    editorial$lejr
  ),
  `Why it matters` = c(
    editorial$why_hospitals,
    paste("Largest CBSA:", top_cbsa, "(", top_cbsa_n, "hospitals)"),
    "Covered-lives scale",
    "Readmission pressure under episode accountability",
    "Volume concentration"
  )
)
knitr::kable(glance)
```

# 03 · Guide narrative (from the website TEAM report)


### Takeaways

- 160 hospitals — Territory 1 roster
- NorCal 51; MN 30; CO 27
- SF Bay 37 hospitals largest CBSA
- Kaiser and Providence multi-site edge
- Links California, Minnesota, Colorado guides

## What is Rainfall Territory 1 under CMS TEAM?

Rainfall Health’s **Territory 1 (NorCal, PNW & Rockies)** contains **160** of the **721** active CMS TEAM-mandated hospitals — **22.2%** of the national roster. The territory stretches from the San Francisco Bay Area and Northern California CBSAs through Oregon and Washington, then inland across Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Utah, and South Dakota, and east into **Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, and Colorado**.

California is **split** between Territory 1 and Territory 2. Territory 1 holds the Northern California CBSAs (**51** hospitals): San Francisco–Oakland–Fremont (37), San Jose–Sunnyvale–Santa Clara (6), Santa Rosa–Petaluma (5), Eureka–Arcata (2), and Crescent City (1). Southern California CBSAs sit in Territory 2. Hospital leaders comparing statewide California guides should treat the NorCal/SoCal split as operationally real for sales coverage and post-acute network design.

Three metros dominate exposure: the **Bay Area** (37), **Denver–Aurora–Centennial** (21), and **Minneapolis–St. Paul–Bloomington** (21). Together they account for nearly half of Territory 1’s hospitals and a disproportionate share of LEJR and spinal-fusion volume.

(Source: [CMS TEAM participant list (March 2026); Rainfall territoryHospitals.json.](https://www.cms.gov/priorities/innovation/innovation-models/team-model))

**Fast facts**

- 160 mandated hospitals (March 2026)
- 12 states + CA NorCal CBSAs
- Top states: California (NorCal) 51 · Minnesota 30 · Colorado 27 · Oregon 17 · Illinois 12 · Wisconsin 11
- Top CBSAs: SF–Oakland 37 · Denver 21 · Minneapolis–St. Paul 21 · Portland 17
- Integrated-system signals: Kaiser Permanente, Providence, UCHealth, Twin Cities nonprofits
- Interactive map: /territory-map

## Which CBSAs concentrate the most TEAM risk?

CMS selected markets at the **CBSA** level. In Territory 1, a handful of metros carry most of the coordination burden — shared SNFs, home-health agencies, and orthopedic groups that serve multiple mandated hospitals.

| CBSA | Hospitals |
| --- | --- |
| San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont, CA | 37 |
| Denver-Aurora-Centennial, CO | 21 |
| Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington, MN-WI | 21 |
| Portland-Vancouver-Hillsboro, OR-WA | 17 |
| San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara, CA | 6 |
| Santa Rosa-Petaluma, CA | 5 |
| Duluth, MN-WI | 5 |
| Peoria, IL | 4 |
| Green Bay, WI | 4 |
| Fort Collins-Loveland, CO | 3 |

## Which health systems are structurally advantaged here?

**Kaiser Permanente** has one of the densest explicit brand footprints on the national TEAM roster (~19 hospitals by name match), with heavy Northern California presence — prepaid integration, employed physicians, and owned post-acute pathways that map cleanly onto 30-day episode accountability.

**Providence** (~9 name-matched TEAM sites) anchors parts of the PNW and Inland West. **UCHealth** and **Intermountain Health** (including former SCL sites) shape Denver’s multi-hospital competition alongside HCA HealthONE facilities that sit in Colorado but compete in the same post-acute market.

In the Twin Cities, **M Health Fairview**, **Allina**, **HealthPartners**, and **Essentia** (Duluth corridor) illustrate the nonprofit-integrated pattern: shared EHRs and employed specialty groups reduce handoff friction that typically inflates SNF and readmission spend under bundles (Dummit et al., 2016; Finkelstein et al., 2021).

## What should Territory 1 hospitals prioritize before downside risk?

Leaders in Bay Area, Denver, Minneapolis–St. Paul, and Portland markets should treat **post-acute network governance** as the primary TEAM workstream — not OR efficiency alone. Shared metro SNFs mean one hospital’s discharge patterns can be undercut by a competitor’s preferred-provider list.

Second, align orthopedic and spine service-line finance with episode-level cost accounting. LEJR remains the volume engine nationally; hip fracture and spinal fusion drive outlier spend. Third, reconcile your hospital’s presence on the March 2026 CMS list against any internal “741” spreadsheet still circulating from September 2024 — see our hospital-count explainer.

For state-level hospital directories, use the California (NorCal section), Minnesota, and Colorado guides, and the interactive territory map at **/territory-map**.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many CMS TEAM hospitals are in Rainfall Territory 1?

160 active hospitals on the March 2026 CMS participant list, including 51 Northern California TEAM hospitals.

### Is all of California in Territory 1?

No. California is split: Territory 1 covers Northern California CBSAs (51 hospitals); Territory 2 covers Southern California CBSAs (56 hospitals).

### What are the largest CBSAs in Territory 1?

San Francisco–Oakland–Fremont (37), Denver–Aurora–Centennial (21), Minneapolis–St. Paul–Bloomington (21), and Portland–Vancouver–Hillsboro (17).

### Which systems matter most in this region?

Kaiser Permanente and Providence for West Coast integration; UCHealth/Intermountain/HCA HealthONE in Denver; Fairview/Allina/HealthPartners in the Twin Cities.

### Where can I see the hospital list on a map?

Rainfall’s interactive CMS TEAM sales territory map at /territory-map filters by territory and state.

# Named hospitals (live roster)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-directory
hospitals |>
  dplyr::group_by(state, cbsa_label) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Hospitals = dplyr::n(),
    `Named hospitals` = paste(hospital, collapse = " · "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(state, dplyr::desc(Hospitals), cbsa_label) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
